title: Milnor exact sequence for a derived inverse limit

from.place: proof, first step, cohomology of the derived inverse limit

statement: Let $(K_n)_{n\geq0}$ be a countable inverse system in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and let $R\varprojlim_nK_n$ be a derived inverse limit [def-weil-derived-limit]. For every integer $i$ there is a natural short exact sequence $$0\to R^1\varprojlim_n H^{i-1}(K_n)\to H^i(R\varprojlim_nK_n)\to\varprojlim_n H^i(K_n)\to0,$$ where $R^1\varprojlim$ denotes the first derived functor of the inverse-limit functor on abelian groups.

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), displayed short exact sequence; More on Algebra, Remark 15.88.5 (Tag 07KY)

proof.text: By the definition of a derived inverse limit, the system has a Roos distinguished triangle $R\varprojlim_nK_n\xrightarrow{p}\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nK_n\to(R\varprojlim_nK_n)[1]$. Countable products in $\operatorname{Ab}$ are exact [lem-pc-abelian-groups-exact-products], so by part (2) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] the product $\prod_nK_n$ exists in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$ and $H^i(\prod_nK_n)\cong\prod_nH^i(K_n)$ via the maps $H^i(\mathrm{pr}_n)$; since $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ(1-s)=\mathrm{pr}_n-f_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$, under this identification $H^i(1-s)$ is the map $1-s$ on $\prod_nH^i(K_n)$ for the inverse system $(H^i(K_n),H^i(f_n))$.

source.place: Tag 07KX, derived-limit distinguished triangle; Tag 07KC, products in the derived category

proof.text: Apply the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to the Roos triangle of Step 1; with Step 1 its segment $\prod_nH^{i-1}(K_n)\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nH^{i-1}(K_n)\to H^i(R\varprojlim_nK_n)\xrightarrow{H^i(p)}\prod_nH^i(K_n)\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nH^i(K_n)$ is exact. By the Roos computation [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups], applied to the inverse systems of abelian groups $(H^{i-1}(K_n))_n$ and $(H^i(K_n))_n$, the kernel of $1-s$ in degree $i$ is $\varprojlim_nH^i(K_n)$ and the cokernel of $1-s$ in degree $i-1$ is naturally $R^1\varprojlim_nH^{i-1}(K_n)$, the first right derived functor of the inverse limit. Exactness therefore gives the short exact sequence $0\to R^1\varprojlim_nH^{i-1}(K_n)\to H^i(R\varprojlim_nK_n)\to\varprojlim_nH^i(K_n)\to0$.
